title: Mixture + Retrieval + Eval: quick annotated learning scratchpad
content:
Purpose: capture quick impressions from recent papers + a few mini-experiments to try. Not polished — mostly bullet thoughts, questions for next sprint, rough sketches for evals.

Context: thinking about combining conditional compute (MoE) ideas with lightweight retrieval layers for cost-effective specialization. Also want to sketch evals that catch degradation modes that simple perplexity checks miss. Useful for product team conversations and potential POC for Redwood Dedicated capacity experiments.

Papers/readings (quick notes):
- "Switch/Conditional compute" family (GShard, Switch Transformers) — arXiv 2021-ish.
  - Key idea: route tokens to experts, huge model capacity with sparse activation. Good for scaling but routing overhead + memory fragmentation.
  - Ops implications: shard parameters across GPUs, need fast all-to-all for activations, careful quantization strategy per-expert.
  - My note: for Dedicated pools, could consider small-number-of-experts colocated per-machine (reduce all-to-all) and use routing policy that prefers local experts for latency predictability.

- "Sparse MoE + structured routing" paper summary (recent workshop notes):
  - Balanced routing (GShard top-k) reduces expert collapse but needs auxiliary loss. Tuning that loss is brittle.
  - Practical tip: deterministic fallback when experts overloaded (fallback to base model). Useful for graceful degradation.

- "RETRO / Retrieval-augmented models" (DeepMind / others)
  - Retrieval gives copy-while-attend mechanism; good for long-tail facts and reducing param count.
  - Index freshness and retrieval latency are the hard parts. For hosted product, region-local indices + async prefetching seemed promising.
  - Combined thought: route to experts specialized on retrieval-augmented contexts vs pure LM contexts. e.g., if query matched a high-sim score, route to retrieval-expert that conditions heavily on KV of external chunks.

- "Routing Transformer / conditional computation with cache-awareness" (conference notes)
  - Idea: routing decisions informed by KV cache similarity to prior context; helps maintain coherence for long documents.
  - Implementation thought: add a lightweight similarity probe in the runtime that flags when to use local cache-optimized paths.

Evaluation ideas (what to measure beyond ppl):
- Latency P95/P99 when routing to local vs remote experts (simulate local-first policy).
- Cost per 1k tokens for mixed workload (50% short chat, 30% long documents, 20% retrieval-heavy queries). Compute capacity + GPU utilization graphs.
- Quality regressions by user-intent slice: factual Q&A, summarization, code generation. Need targeted prompt sets per slice.
- Safety/evasive behavior when expert overload occurs; test fallback outputs — are they coherent or hallucinate?

Mini-experiment pipeline sketches:
- Experiment A: Small MoE prototype on 8x A100: 32 experts but colocate 4 experts per card (simulated local routing). Route policy: softmax top-1 but prefer local with +bias.
  - Metrics: throughput (tokens/s), end-to-end latency, expert utilisation heatmap.
  - Quick TODOs: create synthetic workload with mix above, instrument tracing spans for routing+alltoall.

- Experiment B: Retrieval hybrid: build a tiny index of our internal docs (kb ~ 50k docs). Test whether retrieval to small RAG expert improves exact-match on factoid Qs and reduces generated hallucinations.
  - Evaluation: EM on curated Q set + human spot checks. Measure added latency for retrieval and end-to-end tokens.

- Experiment C: Evals for graceful degradation. Simulate expert OOM and force fallback to compact baseline model. Run prompts that historically trigger stronger hallucinations and see delta in truthfulness scores.

Open questions / risks:
- Routing overhead vs benefit at small scale: if routing adds 10–30% latency overhead, how big must the quality/throughput gain be to justify Dedicated config complexity?
- Quantization per-expert: if experts are quantized differently, can runtime support mixed kernels without huge penalty?
- Index staleness: how to maintain region-local indices with low sync cost? periodic vs event-driven updates?
- Monitoring: what are the right signals to decide when to disable sparse routing for an app (cost spike, latency SLO breaches, degradation on evals)?

Concrete next steps (short list):
- [ ] Prototype routing bias: implement simple local-preference bias in infra PR (low-risk codepath) — assign to Owen. (See linked PR in artifacts)
- [ ] Build small retrieval index from 50k-doc snapshot; run retrieval-augmented vs baseline on our Q set — assign to Nina.
- [ ] Draft canary plan for enabling MoE-like routing in a Dedicated pool (slo rollback, quota controls, fallback). I'll draft the confluence page outline.
- [ ] Define 3 prompt slices and create 200 prompts each for targeted evals (factual QA, summarization, code). Need human labels for truthfulness.

Notes to self (fragmented):
- Could we treat retrieval as a special "expert" that takes whole-doc context as input and returns condensed embeddings for decoder? low-latency path might be tricky.
- Think about placement constraint: co-locate index hot-shards with experts that most often use them. Similar to cache affinity.
- If we pursue this, need to model cost: dedicated GPU hours for experts + storage for indices + networking costs for cross-host alltoall. Put together simple cost model spreadsheet.

Useful links I re-read:
- GShard / Switch transformer arXiv
- RETRO / retrieval-augmented repo
- internal infra PR: /github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/412

Rough timeline thoughts: 2–4 week spike to validate latency/cost tradeoffs, then if promising, build canary with 1 customer on Dedicated (small committed capacity) for 8–12 weeks.

End.
